top.title: Hackers help themselves to 1Password's source code and customer data
top.description: 1Password is reassuring customers that their vaults remain secure after an attacker breached its systems and stole account information and private source code. The Canadian security biz disclosed this week that an attacker had compromised an employee's corporate GitHub account, made off with private source code, and deployed malicious code to its backend services to siphon off customer information. 1Password, which began investigating the intrusion on November 19, hasn't said how many customers were affected, but confirmed that the stolen data includes names and email addresses used to sign in to the service, account identifiers, timestamps showing when users created and last accessed their accounts, and various pieces of non-secret account metadata. The company insists the information that customers actually pay it to protect was beyond the intruder's reach. "At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker," 1Password said. Arguably more troubling is the revelation that the intruder gained access to 1Password's continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) infrastructure, which houses credentials used to keep its products running. The company says it has rotated or revoked potentially exposed credentials and that neither its apps nor its browser extensions were affected. 1Password hasn't explained how access to an employee's GitHub account enabled the attacker to deploy malicious code to its backend services, nor has it detailed the extent of the attacker's access to its software build and distribution infrastructure. The company did not respond to The Register's questions. The miscreant also got their hands on tokens embedded in emails sent to some customers as part of account invitations, provisioning, and recovery processes. These tokens aren't enough to access an account on their own, according to 1Password, as users must also authenticate via single sign-on or enter a verification code sent to their registered email address. The company says it specifically notified the small number of users with affected provisioning or recovery processes underway. It found no internal evidence of account takeovers using the exposed provisioning tokens. Still, the breach has prompted the password management biz to beef up those verification codes, replacing the six-digit numeric variety with ten-character alphanumeric codes to make brute-forcing them considerably more difficult. 1Password has booted the intruder out of its GitHub environment, revoked the stolen token, and rolled back the affected backend services to clean versions of the code. It's since shored up security around its development infrastructure and employees' devices, and brought in outside security specialists to review its handiwork. The incident recalls the first stage of LastPass's 2022 breach, when an attacker compromised its development environment and stole source code. top.title: Space plants with hot sauce: What ISS astronauts will be eating on Thanksgiving (video)
top.description: null The astronauts on the International Space Station will celebrate Thanksgiving with some nontraditional fare. Well, NASA astronaut Anil Menon will, anyway. In a video the agency released on Monday (Nov. 23), Menon showed off some of the plants he and his crewmates are growing in orbit and told us what's in store for the greens. "We need plants to survive as we set up our moon base , and as we go to Mars , we're going to have to grow our own nutrition. So that's what we're doing this Thanksgiving," Menon said in the 2.5-minute video. Astronauts deliver a Thanksgiving message from the International Space Station in November 2026. From left: NASA's Luke Delaney and Anil Menon, the Canadian Space Agency's Joshua Kutryk and NASA's Jessica Watkins. (Image credit: NASA) "I plan on using this [plant] with a tortilla and some pasta and some hot sauce to make my Thanksgiving meal," added Menon, who was wearing a chef's toque for the occasion. "And I'm grateful for you and for my family at home." He passed the microphone to fellow NASA astronaut Luke Delaney, who didn't talk about food but expressed gratitude to his family, crewmates and support network on Earth . Next up was NASA's Jessica Watkins, who gave us a rundown of the broader Thanksgiving menu in space. "Some of what we'll be eating here — we've got some roasted turkey, some mac and cheese, some mashed potatoes, and some candied yams," Watkins said, showing off the small bags containing each of those comestibles. "So, we should be in good shape." The Canadian Space Agency 's (CSA) Joshua Kutryk spoke next. He said he'll eat rice and the space-grown plants, which he'll consume raw "because it reminds me of Earth, which I miss." All four of the astronauts then wished us a happy Thanksgiving and did some zero-g flips and rolls, sending the space plants on a bit of a ride. Delaney, Kutryk and Watkins are members of SpaceX's Crew-13 mission, which arrived at the International Space Station (ISS) on Oct. 1 . There's a fourth Crew-13 astronaut as well — Sergey Teteryatnikov, of the Russian space agency Roscosmos . That quartet shares the ISS with Menon and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina, who arrived in July aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft. Astronauts tend to get major holidays off on the ISS, and to celebrate them together. Doing so reinforces the already-strong bonds the crewmates share and helps them deal with the pain of being away from friends and family, which can be especially acute on holidays like Thanksgiving and Christmas. Kutryk is likely feeling especially emotional these days. On Tuesday, the CSA announced that Kutryk's wife had given birth to the couple's third child, a daughter. "Even with the distance between us, we feel incredibly connected as we welcome our new little star into our lives," the couple said in a statement shared by the CSA. "We are very proud of our growing family and are looking forward to getting our little crew of five all reunited."

top.description: The captains of the 12 teams involved in the Nations Championship line up with the tournament trophy and hemisphere shield [Getty Images] Earlier this year, when planning their Nations Championship finals week, Argentina's staff had a request. Would their hotel in Shepperton allow the team to scorch a patch of the hotel garden for an asado – a traditional Argentine barbecue, in which meat on a low grill is cooked over a bed of hot charcoal? Japan were also making arrangements. The Brave Blossoms had a special rice cooker shipped over to supplement the kitchen facilities at their Kensington base. Such are the countless details that go into an unprecedented logistical juggle. The maths makes the bottleneck clear. The Nations Championship brings together more than 550 players and support staff from the world's top 12 teams for six matches funnelled into three days and just one venue - Twickenham. The new tournament has made new, unprecedented demands on organisers. The first was to find enough accommodation in one corner of London, on a notoriously busy shopping weekend, kicked off by Black Friday sales. A block booking was therefore made back at the start of the year to secure beds in hotels from Brentford, Guildford, Cobham and beyond. Not all those establishments had experience of hosting elite rugby teams. So, chefs and team nutritionists convened to ensure that the hotels were braced with sufficient supplies of eggs, chicken and the rest, to cater for the high-energy, high-protein diets of rugby's best players. The demands continue. While their fellow hotel guests might hit the sights, Nations Championship sides hit the pitch. Individual, private training facilities have had to be sourced for each team, with pitches hired out at local clubs, schools and universities. Teams were given the choice of hotels and training grounds based on their world ranking at the start of the tournament in July, with world number ones South Africa nabbing the Teddington base that usually hosts England's opponents on a regular autumn internationals weekend. The choice is all the more important given the logjam of matches means teams will do their eve-of-match captain's run session at their training ground, rather than, as traditional, at the match venue. To get their players, staff and equipment between hotel, training base and Twickenham itself, organisers have given each team use of four vehicles; a team bus, a people carrier, a van for training kit and a truck for moving scrum machines and other heavy items. Once they finally do arrive, Allianz Stadium, which has hosted Sevens, double-headers and schools finals days in the past, has enough changing rooms to comfortably accommodate four teams at once. top.title: Fernando Alonso to miss Qatar F1 media day with viral illness
top.description: Motorsport photo Fernando Alonso will be absent from Formula 1's media day ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix as he recovers from a "viral infection". The two-time champion will miss the traditional media obligations at the Lusail International Circuit as he aims to return to fitness for first practice on Friday. A statement from his Aston Martin team explained: "Fernando will miss media day today as he continues to recover from a viral infection contracted towards the end of the Las Vegas GP weekend. "He is recovering well, and is planned to return to the paddock on Friday." Alonso failed to finish the race in Las Vegas due to what he described as a broken engine late on at the Nevada showpiece , with the Honda-powered Aston Martin enduring one of its most difficult weekends of the season, given the power-hungry nature of the Strip street circuit. It meant that the Spaniard was unable to add to his tally of seven points, which has seen Aston Martin take its place ahead of newcomer Cadillac in the constructors' standings. F1 arrives in Qatar after a drawn-out saga over whether it would be safe to race in the Middle East amid tension in the region, triggered by war between the United States/Israel and Iran. Lusail Lusail Both the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix were cancelled at the start of the year, though the former later returned to the schedule, albeit racing at Malaysia's Sepang circuit. With safety guarantees in place - and with Liberty-owned MotoGP having raced at Lusail a few weeks prior - F1 confirmed that the Qatar race and next weekend's season finale in Abu Dhabi would run as scheduled to complete a 23-race calendar. top.title: Part of India's Test squad, star cricketer listed as 'Stan Stan' plays local cricket in New Zealand
top.description: India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant took part in a local cricket match in Christchurch on Wednesday, using the opportunity to to keep his eye sharp ahead of the second New Zealand Test starting Friday. Pant, 29, is one of the leading six-hitters in Test cricket history. He has hit 108 sixes in 53 matches, the second-highest tally in the format. Six of those sixes came in the first Test in Wellington last week, where his 128 off 153 balls helped India post a record total of 720/9 in New Zealand. The match ended in a draw. Pant's appearance in a local Last Man Stands match came after he was spotted in central Christchurch. One team, Open House Swingers, were down a player and asked Pant if he would fill in, with the Indian star wasting no time picking up the bat to give them a boost. He turned out for the Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones at Hagley Park. The venue is next to Hagley Oval, where he will represent India in the second Test. Listed as Stan Stan on the scorecard, Pant scored 54 off 21 balls, continuing his run-scoring form in New Zealand. "I saw Rishabh going around on an electric bike," Open House Swingers player Mohammad Safi told the New Zealand Herald. "So I went and stopped him, and we start talking and taking a few photos and stuff, and I asked him, do you want to play cricket for us? "He was like, OK, I'll come and play for you guys. Then he came and padded up, went batting, and smashed a few sixes." — RP17Gang (@RP17Gang) India bowling coach Morne Morkel said he "nearly fell off my chair last night when I saw that". New Zealand captain Tom Latham described Pant's performance as "brilliant". "He's obviously a real character of the game is Rishabh, so it's great for him to give his experience back to the LMS teams." Safi told the New Zealand Herald that the opposition players did not recognise Pant, who was wearing a blue tracksuit. He also said Pant had used his cousin's bat during the match. "He was asking me to basically give him a single and stuff. Obviously, I was smashing longer sixes than him, and then he was like, give me a turn, let me show you how to hit it," Safi said. The Open House Swingers won the match by 16 runs. India's second Test against New Zealand begins on Friday at Hagley Oval. 136182903

top.title: Why the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys play every Thanksgiving
top.description: Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images Thanksgiving football is a loved tradition in America, and the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys are part of the fabric. The Detroit Lions kick off Thanksgiving by hosting the Chicago Bears. It is a tradition each year that the Lions host the first game of the day – but why? Lions started regular Thanksgiving football The Detroit Lions really invented the concept of Thanksgiving football back in 1934. Their owner at the time George A. Richards believed the holiday date could be a good opportunity for ticket sales. Richards had a radio deal with NBC that also allowed the games to be broadcast nationally. Demand for the event was a huge success. While games had been played on Thanksgiving before, it was the Lions who made it a yearly event, and they have been cemented in the schedule ever since. Over the years the Lions’ record is 38-46-2 on Thanksgiving. However, in their last nine games they are 1-8. Dallas Cowboys seized second Thanksgiving slot By 1966 the Detroit Lions’ annual game was televised and, the NFL decided they wanted a second slot. Dallas Cowboys president Tex Schramm volunteered. At the time there were still concerns about playing on a Thursday, with less time to recover, but Schramm felt the financial attraction and home advantage made it worthwhile. With the exception of two years in the 1970s, the Dallas Cowboys have played on Thanksgiving ever since. The NFL added a third Thanksgiving slot in 2006, rotated the schedule each year. The Cowboys’ overall record on Thanksgiving is 35–22–1. top.description: Exeter won two and lost two of their PWR Cup pool matches earlier this season [Shutterstock] New Exeter head coach Oli Bishop feels his side will be title contenders this season in Premiership Women's Rugby. Bishop was promoted to lead the Chiefs over the summer after Steve Salvin left to become forwards coach with Wales. The former Ealing and Wasps coach has spent 13 years coaching in the top flight and takes over an Exeter side that he helped finish third last season before a late 40-38 loss at eventual champions Saracens in the play-off semi-finals. "The girls are in a good place," he told BBC South West. "We're not changing huge amounts of things, our DNA is our DNA. "We've looked to bring in an extra coach, this is the first time Chiefs have had three full-time coaches and I think that's going to make a huge difference to what we can do and the detail we can go to. "So I would say that we're going to be contenders, but I'm also going to say I think this is probably the most competitive season that we're going to see out there this year." Oli Bishop took over as Exeter head coach over the summer [Shutterstock] Exeter have had to wait an extra week to begin their campaign in the nine-team PWR. They start the season with a tough trip to a Bristol side that ran in eight tries in a 48-21 win at Harlequins last week and have brought players including England star Ellie Kildunne and Wales flanker Bethan Lewis. Exeter have kept most of the squad that got them to the final four in June as they prepare to return to league action after the autumn's WXV matches. "A big thing for us is continuity and cohesion," Bishop added. "We're really happy with the squad and staff that we have and that's why we kept as many as we could at the end of the season. "So we'll be looking to build, we'll be looking to try and do things slightly differently, but again keep our DNA and keep our identity how we want that to be. "Me and Steve worked a lot last year on the culture and identity of this place and how we would change things from the previous way it was being run. "I was 100% on board with that, I've made a couple of tweaks here and there, but they're small changes. "I'm wanting the girls to go out on the weekend and be brave, take the opportunities that are there and be able to express themselves with a clear understanding of how our DNA influences the way that we play."

During their time as players Brady won a record seven Super Bowl championships, while Manning picked up two. However, Manning had the upper hand on the MVP front, securing the award on five occasions compared to three for Brady. Two greats of the sport going head-to-head for over a decade, of course, led to some tension on the field. But it is in their post-careers that they seem to have become much closer. Tom Brady admits he and Peyton Manning are ‘much better friends now’ Speaking on Fox Sports this week, Brady was asked: “Mahomes-Allen really feels like Brady-Manning to me. top.title: Kentucky Football seeing good ROI on roster spend
top.description: There’s no getting around the fact that Kentucky hasn’t won a football game since Oct. 24, when the Wildcats toppled Vanderbilt 34-17 in Lexington. top.title: Gunmen kill 16, injure four in overnight attack on Plateau community
top.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos No fewer than 16 persons, including women, youths and children, have been killed after gunmen stormed Tafi Gana community, a hamlet of Kyie Ihwien, near Jebbu Miango in Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State. The attack, according to the Irigwe Development Association (IDA), occurred at about 11:30pm on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, leaving four other persons injured and throwing the community into confusion, fear and panic. The association, in a statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Sam Jugo, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Thursday, said, “The attackers wielded assault rifles and other dangerous weapons.” “They stormed the community and started shooting sporadically.” It added, “By dawn of Thursday, November 26, 2026, about 16 persons lay dead, while four other survivors were rushed to unknown medical facilities with various degrees of injuries.” The association gave the names of those killed as Moses Oko, 70; Maingwa Zere Rangya, 60; Danladi Ishaku, 45; Luka Danladi, 21; Elisha Luka, 18; David Danladi, 10; Ishaya Goslow, 18; Lami Danladi, 30; Isi Ishaku, 18; Zhime Ngaza, 75; ThankGod Danladi, 18; Gideon Joseph, 25; Ladi Abba, 65; Ruth Istifanus, 20; Mary Keyi, 18; and Lazarus Musa, 13. The statement quoted the traditional ruler of the area, Nggwe Gado Dama, as confirming the incident, adding that the matter had been reported to security agencies. It said, “The matter had been reported to security operatives who were, as at press time, at the scene of the attack.” The association condemned the killings and appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid taking the law into their hands. It said, “The IDA appeals to all natives not to take laws into their hands but allow the security agencies to do the needful to dispense justice to the slain.” The association expressed condolences to the bereaved families and the entire Irigwe nation, praying for the repose of the souls of the victims and God’s comfort for their immediate families. The Green Bay Packers watched their second-half offense unravel during Wednesday night’s 26-13 Thanksgiving Eve loss to the Los Angeles Rams , and head coach Matt LaFleur did not sugarcoat what went wrong through the air. Speaking postgame to broadcaster Larry McCarren, LaFleur offered his assessment of both costly turnovers. “There was one miscommunication, the last one. Trailing 20-13 late in the third quarter, Packers linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper intercepted Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford and returned it 21 yards to give Love prime field position. Two plays later, Love fired deep toward the end zone for wide receiver Matthew Golden. Rams safety Jaylen McCollough read the play and hauled in the interception at the 17-yard line. Green Bay got one final life late in the fourth quarter, trailing 23-13 after converting a fourth-and-8 on a 12-yard pass to wide receiver Bo Melton. On the very next snap, Love launched another deep shot for Melton, and Rams cornerback Emmanuel Forbes Jr. snagged the game-sealing pick. Without Watson, who caught four passes for 65 yards and a 6-yard touchdown before his injury, Love managed just 44 passing yards after halftime. Meanwhile, Green Bay rushed for 55 yards and held the ball for only 19:20 as Rams running back Blake Corum piled up 184 yards and a touchdown on 32 carries. Now sitting at 6-5 after two straight losses, LaFleur and Love have plenty of offensive kinks to clean up fast. nigeria.title: Mr Latin hands over TAMPAN presidency after eight years
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nollywood actor, Bolaji Amusan, popularly known as Mr Latin, has stepped down as president of the Theatre Arts and Motion Pictures Practitioners Association of Nigeria (TAMPAN) after eight years in office. Amusan handed over the association’s leadership to his successor, Ajala Jalingo, at a transition ceremony, announcing the development in a post on his Instagram page on Wednesday. Sharing a video of the handover, the actor described the occasion as the end of his eight year tenure as the association’s Global President. “Today, I officially handed over the TAMPAN flag to my successor, @ajala_jalingo, bringing my eight-year tenure as Global President to a close,” he wrote. Amusan, who became president in December 2018 following the resignation of his predecessor, Dele Odule, was re-elected unopposed in December 2022 for another four-year term. Although he has left the presidency, the actor will remain involved in the association as a member of its Board of Trustees. “I bow out with gratitude, honour and fulfilment, while embracing a new responsibility as a distinguished member of the prestigious Board of Trustees (BOT) of TAMPAN,” he added. He also expressed confidence in the association’s future under Jalingo’s leadership, saying the change in administration would not affect its commitment to service and development. “Leadership may change, but commitment to service and the growth of TAMPAN remains unwavering,” Amusan said. TAMPAN represents theatre and film practitioners across Nigeria, particularly those in the Yoruba movie industry. The association works to promote members’ interests and welfare, as well as the development of the entertainment sector. Amusan began his acting career in 1988 and is known for his comic roles in Yoruba films. He has also worked as a filmmaker and producer. nigeria.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. When playing games online, a player chooses a payment method, enters their required details and they often see the funds appear in their account within a matter of seconds. When the time comes when the player wants to withdraw their money , it can be a very different experience. The request may remain pending for hours before additional processing and banking delays extend the wait across several days. That contrast naturally causes frustration. If a platform can accept money instantly, why can it not return money at the same speed. The answer involves more than payment technology. Withdrawals move through security checks, internal approval processes, payment providers, and banking systems that deposits may not encounter in the same way. Deposits and Withdrawals Are Not Mirror Images A deposit is designed to confirm that funds are available and can be transferred successfully. Payment networks can authorize many card and digital wallet transactions almost immediately. Once authorization is received, the casino can credit the player’s balance, even if the complete financial settlement happens later. A withdrawal requires the platform to release funds from its own system. Before doing so, the operator may need to confirm the player’s identity, verify account ownership, review transaction history, and check whether promotional conditions have been satisfied. The payment must then be approved and sent through an eligible withdrawal method. This difference means that an instant deposit does not prove that an instant withdrawal is technically or operationally possible. However, it also does not excuse operators that create unnecessary obstacles or fail to communicate their procedures clearly. Verification Can Become the First Bottleneck Identity verification is one of the most common reasons for a delayed withdrawal. Casinos may request proof of identity, proof of address, or evidence showing that the payment method belongs to the account holder. nigeria.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo refused to let assassinated Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi’s delegation bring high-powered weapons into Abuja in 2006, a decision he said saved lives. Fani-Kayode, a former minister of aviation, gave the account in a Facebook post titled “20 Years Ago With Muammar Ghaddafi!” who had then arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit. He said he received the Libyan leader at the airport on Obasanjo’s behalf and was detailed to accompany him for four days. “He arrived at the airport with no less than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja. The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the convoy was blocked at the gate by Nigerian security personnel and the military. He said Gaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in with their sidearms, but not the weapons in the boots of the vehicles. After three more failed attempts to leave, he said, the Libyan leader lost his temper. “Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!” he said. He said he called Obasanjo, who was on his way to the airport to travel to Lagos, and told Gaddafi the President was coming to settle the matter himself. Gaddafi agreed to return to the airport. Fani-Kayode said Obasanjo greeted Gaddafi warmly, apologised for the blockage and promised that the gates would be opened. But as he left, the then President whispered an instruction to him. “As he walked past me he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK 47’s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane,” he said. He said Gaddafi’s Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol had threatened to fly the Libyan leader home and boycott the entire conference if the weapons were not allowed in. The Libyan officials complied after what he described as a “hot encounter and harsh trading of words”. nigeria.title: Musk To Give Two SpaceX Shares To ‘Every Child In America’
nigeria.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. The world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year. He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work. APRIL 30: Elon Musk arrives to court at the Ronald V. Dellums Federal Building on April 30, 2026 in Oakland, California. (Photo by Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP “I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.” “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said. In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.” There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau. The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion. SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion. nigeria.description: The Katsina State Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) for the 2027 general elections, Senator Ahmad Babba Kaita, has described the forthcoming polls as a crucial battle that Nigerians must pursue with determination and collective strength. Senator Kaita made the declaration while continuing his campaign tour across the Funtua Zone, where he sought the support and confidence of voters ahead of the 2027 elections. Addressing supporters during the campaign engagements, the former federal lawmaker said only Nigerians who are directly affected by governance challenges can fully explain the difficulties facing the country, arguing that the electorate has the power to determine the direction of the nation through their votes. According to him, the growing enthusiasm witnessed during ADC campaigns, including those led by the party’s presidential candidate and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, demonstrates Nigerians’ desire for a new political direction. Kaita said the reception accorded the ADC across the country, including Katsina State, shows that citizens are prepared to use the ballot box to pursue what he described as positive change. The ADC governorship candidate also disclosed that candidates of the party from the seven North-West states have agreed to implement a common development agenda focused on tackling insecurity, improving education, boosting agriculture, strengthening healthcare delivery, expanding economic opportunities and promoting social development. On his plans for Katsina State, Senator Kaita reiterated his commitment to granting full autonomy to local government areas within his first six months in office if elected. He said his administration would conduct local government elections within the first three months, describing grassroots governance as a critical foundation for effective development. However, Kaita warned that local government administrations and other government institutions under his leadership would be subjected to strict monitoring to prevent abuse and mismanagement of public resources. “We will establish a state-owned Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) that will ensure the judicious management of our resources for the benefit of the people of Katsina State,” he assured. In a statement issued by the Spokesman of Kaita, the ADC campaign train is currently touring the 11 local government areas of Funtua Zone, attracting large crowds of supporters across towns and villages. nigeria.title: Protesters, FIFA boss, Democrat, spy: People who helped define 2026
nigeria.description: Of the many people who made their mark on 2026, five in particular stand out — from an alleged Chinese spy to FIFA’s troubled president and a Madrid pensioner who became the face of Spain’s housing protests. – Alice Huang – She’s the woman at the heart of the international espionage scandal whose ripple effects are still emerging. Suspected of spying for Beijing, Alice Huang flew under the radar until the explosive revelation of her affair with the chief of US chip giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang. The outcry saw him resign, before being sensationally reinstated just days later after the intervention of US President Donald Trump. Alice Huang — no relation to the leather jacket-clad Jensen — is a former director of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing company under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese tech firms obtain Nvidia AI chips in violation of US export controls. China denies the spying allegations. Alice Huang has not been seen since the scandal erupted. Details on her life are murky, but the Chinese citizen with a Hong Kong passport was filmed at a Taipei party in 2025 wearing a pink dress as she kissed Jensen Huang on the cheek. His departure on November 12 tanked Nvidia’s market value, sparking infighting within the Trump administration over what officials knew, and raising the spectre of trade clashes with China as the US tightens export controls of advanced AI chips. Nvidia’s shares rose 30 percent after the tech giant announced on November 23 that it had reinstated Huang, with Trump saying he had spoken to the board “directly”, igniting a political backlash and leaving many questions unanswered. – Gianni Infantino – FIFA President Gianni Infantino oversaw a highly successful World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico, even brushing off a controversial episode when USA forward Folarin Balogun had his red card suspended following a direct appeal by Trump. But football is a game of highs and lows, and within weeks Infantino faced calls to stand down over plans to sell stakes in World Cup commercial rights to a company run by the brother of Trump’s son-in-law. The proposal was hastily dropped following opposition led by European confederation UEFA, leaving Infantino’s re-election plans in March 2027 in peril. French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo was UEFA’s late choice as candidate. nigeria.title: US lists 63 professions eligible for 3-year work visa
nigeria.description: The US has outlined 63 professional categories whose qualified practitioners can apply for a temporary work visa allowing them to take up employment in the country for up to three years. The arrangement, known as the Trade National (TN) visa, is available exclusively to citizens of Canada and Mexico under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). The TN visa allows eligible professionals from the two neighbouring countries to work for US employers in specified occupations, provided they meet the educational, professional and employment requirements attached to their chosen fields. According to the US Department of State, applicants must be citizens of either Canada or Mexico, have a profession recognised under the USMCA list, secure a prearranged job with a US employer and possess the qualifications required for the position. The list covers several professional sectors, including healthcare, engineering, science, education, accounting and other specialised occupations. Some of the professions recognised under the arrangement include accountants, architects, engineers, lawyers, pharmacists, registered nurses, dentists, veterinarians, economists, mathematicians, scientists, university lecturers and computer systems analysts. Other eligible occupations include agriculturalists, biologists, chemists, geologists, meteorologists, psychologists, social workers, urban planners and technical publications writers. However, appearing on the list does not automatically guarantee approval, as applicants must demonstrate that they satisfy the specific educational or professional requirements for their occupations. Most of the listed professions require a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent, although some categories permit alternative qualifications or professional credentials. The US government also requires applicants to provide details of their proposed employment, including their job responsibilities, expected duration of stay, qualifications and remuneration arrangements. Under Section 214.6 of Title 8 of the US Code of Federal Regulations, successful TN applicants can be admitted into the country for a period not exceeding three years. The classification can also be extended, subject to the applicant continuing to meet the relevant requirements. The application process differs slightly between the two eligible nationalities. Canadian citizens can generally apply for TN status at a US port of entry or designated pre-clearance facility without first obtaining a TN visa from a US embassy. Mexican citizens, however, must obtain a TN nonimmigrant visa from a US embassy or consulate before seeking admission into the country. The arrangement was originally introduced under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which came into force in 1994. It was retained when the USMCA replaced NAFTA on July 1, 2020. nigeria.title: ‘We will find a way to win’ insists Pochettino after rocky Man Utd start
nigeria.description: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino insisted his team would find a way to win games after a tricky start to life at the helm of the Red Devils. United were held to a chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, after a 4-0 thrashing by rivals Liverpool in his first match on Sunday. Man United, 19th in the Premier League, were upset with several refereeing decisions across both matches, but Pochettino said his team had to take responsibility for their situation. “I’m happy to be here,” said Pochettino, when asked about the various decisions that had gone against his team in his first week in charge. “We are here to take responsibility… we are going for sure to improve and to put that team in the place that, because of their history, we deserve to be. “Nothing is easy but we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and most importantly the players and the power and the energy from our fans that is massive and I think united, all together, I think we will find a way to perform and win games.” United had two goals controversially ruled out against Sporting, but might have won the game were it not for a mistake from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. The Belgian dropped the ball for Colombian striker Luis Suarez to score his second goal of the night, cancelling out Bruno Fernandes’s double against his old side. Lammens also saved a Suarez penalty and then gave away a second penalty, this time scored by the striker. “This type of thing happens, that is football,” said Pochettino. “Football is about making mistakes — I’m going to support always my player if something happens.” The Argentine said Man United’s defenders might have done better to help protect Lammens before he spilled the ball. “When you are a ‘keeper, it’s not easy, that ball. entertainment.description: After more than 30 years of experience in the fashion industry, the entrepreneur is bringing her experience to a Nigerian clothing brand built on a simple proposition: quality should not have to come at an exorbitant price. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. Guests explored the space, examined the clothing and made purchases. Yet, amid the excitement of the launch, two observations kept coming up: the quality of the pieces and their affordability. It was a response that reflected the thinking behind HÉYCH, a brand seeking to occupy an important space in the market by making well-made, stylish clothing accessible without asking consumers to compromise on quality. For Ebigbeyi, this approach is informed by more than three decades of experience in the fashion industry. Having spent over 30 years understanding the business of clothing, she brings to HÉYCH a perspective that extends beyond trends and aesthetics to the practical realities of production, pricing and delivering value. “One thing that sets HÉYCH apart is that we do not compromise on quality, and we are equally intentional about making our products affordable. With over 30 years of experience in this industry, I understand the importance of quality, production standards and delivering value to customers,” she says. Rethinking How Fashion Is Produced That understanding is reflected in one of the brand’s most significant decisions: its investment in local manufacturing. Behind HÉYCH’s retail offering is a manufacturing facility in Lagos, a strategic investment that gives the brand greater control over production while creating the capacity to fulfil orders in large quantities. For Ebigbeyi, local production is as much about business efficiency as it is about building something sustainable within Nigeria. Importation can introduce several layers of cost and complexity, from logistics and shipping to delays and quality-control challenges. Creators picked up practical tips in sessions with Victoire, Ifeoma Udeme and Canva. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. sports.description: The captains of the 12 teams involved in the Nations Championship line up with the tournament trophy and hemisphere shield [Getty Images] Earlier this year, when planning their Nations Championship finals week, Argentina's staff had a request. Would their hotel in Shepperton allow the team to scorch a patch of the hotel garden for an asado – a traditional Argentine barbecue, in which meat on a low grill is cooked over a bed of hot charcoal? Japan were also making arrangements. The Brave Blossoms had a special rice cooker shipped over to supplement the kitchen facilities at their Kensington base. Such are the countless details that go into an unprecedented logistical juggle. The maths makes the bottleneck clear. The Nations Championship brings together more than 550 players and support staff from the world's top 12 teams for six matches funnelled into three days and just one venue - Twickenham. The new tournament has made new, unprecedented demands on organisers. The first was to find enough accommodation in one corner of London, on a notoriously busy shopping weekend, kicked off by Black Friday sales. A block booking was therefore made back at the start of the year to secure beds in hotels from Brentford, Guildford, Cobham and beyond. Not all those establishments had experience of hosting elite rugby teams. So, chefs and team nutritionists convened to ensure that the hotels were braced with sufficient supplies of eggs, chicken and the rest, to cater for the high-energy, high-protein diets of rugby's best players. The demands continue. While their fellow hotel guests might hit the sights, Nations Championship sides hit the pitch. Individual, private training facilities have had to be sourced for each team, with pitches hired out at local clubs, schools and universities. Teams were given the choice of hotels and training grounds based on their world ranking at the start of the tournament in July, with world number ones South Africa nabbing the Teddington base that usually hosts England's opponents on a regular autumn internationals weekend. The choice is all the more important given the logjam of matches means teams will do their eve-of-match captain's run session at their training ground, rather than, as traditional, at the match venue. To get their players, staff and equipment between hotel, training base and Twickenham itself, organisers have given each team use of four vehicles; a team bus, a people carrier, a van for training kit and a truck for moving scrum machines and other heavy items. sports.title: Why the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys play every Thanksgiving
sports.description: Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images Thanksgiving football is a loved tradition in America, and the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys are part of the fabric. The Detroit Lions kick off Thanksgiving by hosting the Chicago Bears. It is a tradition each year that the Lions host the first game of the day – but why? Lions started regular Thanksgiving football The Detroit Lions really invented the concept of Thanksgiving football back in 1934. Their owner at the time George A. Richards believed the holiday date could be a good opportunity for ticket sales. Richards had a radio deal with NBC that also allowed the games to be broadcast nationally. Demand for the event was a huge success. While games had been played on Thanksgiving before, it was the Lions who made it a yearly event, and they have been cemented in the schedule ever since. Over the years the Lions’ record is 38-46-2 on Thanksgiving. However, in their last nine games they are 1-8. Dallas Cowboys seized second Thanksgiving slot By 1966 the Detroit Lions’ annual game was televised and, the NFL decided they wanted a second slot. Dallas Cowboys president Tex Schramm volunteered. At the time there were still concerns about playing on a Thursday, with less time to recover, but Schramm felt the financial attraction and home advantage made it worthwhile. With the exception of two years in the 1970s, the Dallas Cowboys have played on Thanksgiving ever since. The NFL added a third Thanksgiving slot in 2006, rotated the schedule each year. The Cowboys’ overall record on Thanksgiving is 35–22–1. sports.description: Wednesday results boost Arsenal’s Champions League hopes There were a few positive results from an Arsenal perspective in Wednesday night’s Champions League clashes, keeping the Gunners in the top eight. PSG remain two points ahead of Arsenal, but their first dropped points has kept the door open for a possible slip-up later. If Arsenal can catch PSG and steal a top-two spot, they’d be grateful for it later. But they currently sit in seventh, so there’s plenty of work to do. The key thing is remaining in the top eight, and avoiding an extra two-legged play-off tie in February. 16 points has always been enough to make the top-eight in previous seasons, so Arsenal need another five points in their final three games. One win and two draws would do it, with the Gunners to face Real Madrid (H), Real Betis (A), and Sabah (H) in their final three. Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images

sports.title: ‘For another second’ – Ryan Clark suggests Mike McCarthy should be fired from Steelers job
sports.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images After listening to Aaron Rodgers’ account of what has been going on with Mike McCarthy, Ryan Clark suggests it might be time for the Steelers to move on from him. Ryan Clark won a Super Bowl as a part of the Pittsburgh Steelers. The legendary safety was known for his tough-tackling ways during his time with the franchise, and has made quite the media career for himself since retiring from the National Football League. So he has some authority when he speaks about the Steelers, to say the least. There is no escaping the latest fiasco unfolding following Aaron Rodgers’ unbelievable interview about head coach Mike McCarthy. And while Rodgers is already out of Pittsburgh, Clark thinks the other half of the beef should also be removed soon. Ryan Clark says Aaron Rodgers’ account being corroborated by others should see Mike McCarthy sacked The Steelers have been known to be one of the most sound and stable franchises in the NFL for decades. One of the most storied organisations in the sport’s history, they have claimed six Super Bowl titles and laid a foundation of success in Pittsburgh. And it is that legacy to which Clark has appealed when suggesting that McCarthy might just need to lose his job considering everything that has come to light. “I don’t know the financial ramifications or the details of Mike McCarthy’s contract, but Aaron Rodgers’ account has been corroborated by others,” Clark wrote on X. “If that’s the case, I don’t know how the Steelers’ brass allows McCarthy to remain the head coach of one of the NFL’s most storied franchises for another second!” The exact financial figures in terms of how much the Steelers are paying McCarthy is unknown, but he signed a 5-year deal with the franchise at the start of this year. Moving on from him is likely to be fairly expensive. With Rodgers already being released, the issues should simmer down. Although if he really has lost the locker room, it will be very difficult for McCarthy to come back from this. sports.title: Report – Up to three clubs considering January loan move for 18-year-old Barcelona winger
sports.description: Report – Up to three clubs considering January loan move for 18-year-old Barcelona winger Barcelona could face a crucial decision over Jesse Bisiwu’s future during the January transfer window, with up to three European clubs making contact over a possible loan for the young Belgian winger. The discussions come just months after Bisiwu joined Barcelona’s youth setup as part of the club’s international recruitment strategy. However, there is no clarity yet that Barcelona have decided to loan him out, and the club is not currently planning his departure. sports.title: Former Deontay Wilder coach predicts Martin Bakole fight and future Anthony Joshua clash

sports.title: Eli Manning reacts to Aaron Rodgers comments after being benched by the Steelers
sports.description: Photo by Megan Briggs/TGL/TGL Golf via Getty Images Aaron Rodgers has been the talk of the NFL world on the back of initially being benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers before he was released late on Wednesday. On the back of his benching, the veteran quarterback appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and had a lot to say about Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. Eli Manning has since given his take on the situation saying Rodgers is ‘kind of throwing everybody under the bus’. sports.title: Joshua Kimmich calls out club’s handling of Jamal Musiala as ‘not Bayern-like’
sports.description: Joshua Kimmich has criticised Bayern Munich over their handling of teammate Jamal Musiala , describing the club’s public conduct towards the midfielder — who suffers from a neurological condition that causes seizures — as "not Bayern-like". The comments follow public criticism from senior figures at Bayern regarding Musiala’s performances and contract. The player experienced two seizures on the pitch during pre-season fixtures, prompting opposition from the international players' union , FIFPRO. A key squad member has now spoken out, warning that the club risks damaging its traditional family values. "What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public," Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday. "It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either." Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's ongoing struggles were more closely linked to physical injuries over the past two years, including a badly fractured leg at last year's Club World Cup, rather than his medical condition. "It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself," Kimmich added. Musiala and Kimmich are both club and national teammates (Getty) Bayern met with Musiala's representatives on Tuesday to clarify the timeline of events, rejecting speculation that the midfielder concealed his health condition prior to signing his recent contract extension. Both the club and Musiala's representatives accept that he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after extending his contract. "This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared," Bayern said. Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the pitch during two pre-season matches, alarming fans and fellow professionals. Bayern coach Vincent Kompany stated at the time that the episodes were triggered by a change in Musiala's medication. He was rested for the start of the campaign and has since missed games due to a muscle injury. Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Wednesday's defeat at Lille, capping a difficult week for Bayern. Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle on Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern have lost the lead in the Bundesliga and fallen to 15th in the Champions League standings.

technology.title: Hackers help themselves to 1Password's source code and customer data
technology.description: 1Password is reassuring customers that their vaults remain secure after an attacker breached its systems and stole account information and private source code. The Canadian security biz disclosed this week that an attacker had compromised an employee's corporate GitHub account, made off with private source code, and deployed malicious code to its backend services to siphon off customer information. 1Password, which began investigating the intrusion on November 19, hasn't said how many customers were affected, but confirmed that the stolen data includes names and email addresses used to sign in to the service, account identifiers, timestamps showing when users created and last accessed their accounts, and various pieces of non-secret account metadata. The company insists the information that customers actually pay it to protect was beyond the intruder's reach. "At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker," 1Password said. Arguably more troubling is the revelation that the intruder gained access to 1Password's continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) infrastructure, which houses credentials used to keep its products running. The company says it has rotated or revoked potentially exposed credentials and that neither its apps nor its browser extensions were affected. 1Password hasn't explained how access to an employee's GitHub account enabled the attacker to deploy malicious code to its backend services, nor has it detailed the extent of the attacker's access to its software build and distribution infrastructure. The company did not respond to The Register's questions. The miscreant also got their hands on tokens embedded in emails sent to some customers as part of account invitations, provisioning, and recovery processes. These tokens aren't enough to access an account on their own, according to 1Password, as users must also authenticate via single sign-on or enter a verification code sent to their registered email address. The company says it specifically notified the small number of users with affected provisioning or recovery processes underway. It found no internal evidence of account takeovers using the exposed provisioning tokens. Still, the breach has prompted the password management biz to beef up those verification codes, replacing the six-digit numeric variety with ten-character alphanumeric codes to make brute-forcing them considerably more difficult. 1Password has booted the intruder out of its GitHub environment, revoked the stolen token, and rolled back the affected backend services to clean versions of the code. It's since shored up security around its development infrastructure and employees' devices, and brought in outside security specialists to review its handiwork. The incident recalls the first stage of LastPass's 2022 breach, when an attacker compromised its development environment and stole source code. technology.title: 45°C inlets just killed the chiller. Most people haven't noticed yet
technology.description: SC25 in St. Louis looked like a plumbing convention cross booked the supercomputing hall. Pipes, pumps, manifolds, quick-disconnects, and a lot of people who clearly spend more time thinking about pressure drop than floating-point. I kept expecting to see a booth selling industrial fire hoses. Chicago is a much bigger building – McCormick has roughly four times the exhibit space St. Louis had – so the pre-show question was whether SC26 will still look like that or whether the hall is large enough to dilute the effect. If anything, cooling was even more dominant in Chicago. The heat problem didn't get smaller just because the building got bigger. We also saw a lot of new companies displaying their cooling wares at SC26. I follow this stuff closely and see two broad trends. First: consolidation with big industrial suppliers buying up the liquid cooling pioneers. Second: anyone with an angle is heading into the market. Both trends were visible on the floor in Chicago, and everyone had something to say about higher inlet temperatures, whether they have a real story or not. Game changing news The real news, though, is a number Nvidia dropped earlier this year: 45°C (113°F) liquid inlet temperature for their parts. That's not a small tweak. Most liquid-cooled systems have been living in the 30-35°C (86-95°F) world because that's what the chips would tolerate. Jump to 45°C (113°F) and a whole bunch of datacenters that currently need chillers suddenly don't. If AMD, Intel, and the Arm folks can match it – and we’d be shocked if they aren't already working on exactly that – then free cooling stops being a cool climate thing and becomes the default for a lot of places. Rooftop dry coolers can reject nearly any incoming fluid temperature and bring it below 45°C (113°F). There are few places in the world where ambient temperatures approach 113°F, and for the hours when outside temps spike, adiabatic assist is available. This is where water is trickled through a mesh surrounding the dry coolers, which drops the effective temperature another 10–20 percent. So, in our new cooling world, there are two closed loops: one taking heat from the server gear and then passing it to a second, different loop that takes the hot water to the roof, cools it, then brings it back again. What's missing here? It's the chillers. You won't need them anymore. These are essentially huge rooftop refrigerators that cool water even more after the dry cooling. They're expensive, need a lot of maintenance, gulp electricity and are thankfully unnecessary now for new datacenter builds. The power and water savings are not trivial. Legacy designs that rely on chillers and open evaporative towers commonly put 20 percent to 40 percent of total facility energy into cooling. A large share of that is the chiller plant itself – compressors, pumps, and cooling-tower fans. Move to dry coolers running at 45°C (113°F) inlet and that slice collapses. technology.title: UK Home Office waved through border system without a working fix for bad data
technology.description: The Information Commission's Office (ICO) has reprimanded the UK Home Office over a border watchlist system launched without an effective way to correct inaccurate personal information. The regulator said the failings risked people being wrongly detained for additional checks at the UK border, potentially causing distress and other harm. The platform in question, Helios, was slated to replace its predecessor, Warnings Index, in September 2024 and despite an initial delay due to concerns over data quality, went live the following month. Both Helios and Warnings Index are watch-listing systems, designed to allow law enforcement officials – mainly but not exclusively Border Force – to check people's data against official records at the UK border. Helios's federated operating model, whereby the data sources are not centrally managed, yielded quicker results than Warnings Index, but contained a critical flaw in that operational staff could not alter incorrect records. Platform operators, such as Border Force officers, could not amend the data that feeds into it, neither after the fact nor in real time. This was not the case with Warnings Index, which had a dedicated team responsible for correcting data entries in real time. Under Helios, staff were supposed to report inaccuracies to the organization responsible for the relevant source data, which would make the correction. One slight problem: there was no established reporting system at the time Helios was launched on October 2. The platform went live anyway, as officials deemed the data integrity and security risks presented by Warnings Index to be greater than those of Helios. Just nine days passed before the Home Office's data protection officer had to submit a breach report after Helios operational staff said they didn't know how to request data corrections. During the time, Helios operators sent 87 data rectification requests to the Warnings Index correction team, despite it having no capability to make the required changes to the data. The Home Office later said that many other requests likely weren't logged as the proper processes were not in place, and that staff should have logged the issue through a ServiceNow IT ticket, as any other departmental civil servant with any kind of IT issue would have. But the Home Office also said that including personal data in those helpdesk tickets would itself constitute a data breach. The ICO said in its reprimand document [PDF] that it is "unclear" how such a reporting arrangement could realistically work in practice, given that a report would require details from a subject's record that required rectification as well as the new, accurate information that should be used to replace it. technology.title: India’s government ponders cradle to grave AI oversight
technology.description: Indian politicians have proposed that AI could take a major role in citizens’ lives, partly through pervasive surveillance. Prime Minister Narendra Modi last week spelled out his vision for an AI-based app that would collect data about children as they grow and analyze it to determine their aptitude for different types of study or careers. Modi suggested that parents of three-year-old children should enter data about their offspring’s activities and accomplishments into a government-run system that is also accessible to teachers and even a child’s friends. Those records, the PM suggested, will “help identify children's interests and aptitude from an early age and redirect them in the study of their choice in future.” That’s not an entirely creepy idea, because gaining access to India’s top tertiary institutions requires students to pay a hefty fee to sit for entrance exams. Modi pitched recommendations from the AI-powered app as something parents will appreciate as they contemplate whether to fund their offspring’s studies. India’s most populous state, Uttar Pradesh (UP), has proposed to build an “AI Stack” to serve its 240 million-plus residents. The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.” The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create. Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained. Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites. Google, ironically, is a little further along than SpaceX, having launched a test sat in October and last week announcing it has hired Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin to launch a larger satellite carrying the equivalent of a full datacenter rack in early 2029. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. science.title: Space plants with hot sauce: What ISS astronauts will be eating on Thanksgiving (video)
science.description: null The astronauts on the International Space Station will celebrate Thanksgiving with some nontraditional fare. Well, NASA astronaut Anil Menon will, anyway. In a video the agency released on Monday (Nov. 23), Menon showed off some of the plants he and his crewmates are growing in orbit and told us what's in store for the greens. "We need plants to survive as we set up our moon base , and as we go to Mars , we're going to have to grow our own nutrition. So that's what we're doing this Thanksgiving," Menon said in the 2.5-minute video. Astronauts deliver a Thanksgiving message from the International Space Station in November 2026. From left: NASA's Luke Delaney and Anil Menon, the Canadian Space Agency's Joshua Kutryk and NASA's Jessica Watkins. (Image credit: NASA) "I plan on using this [plant] with a tortilla and some pasta and some hot sauce to make my Thanksgiving meal," added Menon, who was wearing a chef's toque for the occasion. "And I'm grateful for you and for my family at home." He passed the microphone to fellow NASA astronaut Luke Delaney, who didn't talk about food but expressed gratitude to his family, crewmates and support network on Earth . Next up was NASA's Jessica Watkins, who gave us a rundown of the broader Thanksgiving menu in space. "Some of what we'll be eating here — we've got some roasted turkey, some mac and cheese, some mashed potatoes, and some candied yams," Watkins said, showing off the small bags containing each of those comestibles. "So, we should be in good shape." The Canadian Space Agency 's (CSA) Joshua Kutryk spoke next. He said he'll eat rice and the space-grown plants, which he'll consume raw "because it reminds me of Earth, which I miss." All four of the astronauts then wished us a happy Thanksgiving and did some zero-g flips and rolls, sending the space plants on a bit of a ride. Delaney, Kutryk and Watkins are members of SpaceX's Crew-13 mission, which arrived at the International Space Station (ISS) on Oct. 1 . There's a fourth Crew-13 astronaut as well — Sergey Teteryatnikov, of the Russian space agency Roscosmos . That quartet shares the ISS with Menon and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina, who arrived in July aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft. Astronauts tend to get major holidays off on the ISS, and to celebrate them together. Doing so reinforces the already-strong bonds the crewmates share and helps them deal with the pain of being away from friends and family, which can be especially acute on holidays like Thanksgiving and Christmas. Kutryk is likely feeling especially emotional these days. On Tuesday, the CSA announced that Kutryk's wife had given birth to the couple's third child, a daughter. "Even with the distance between us, we feel incredibly connected as we welcome our new little star into our lives," the couple said in a statement shared by the CSA. "We are very proud of our growing family and are looking forward to getting our little crew of five all reunited."

science.description: Alzheimer’s disease, involving amyloid plaques in the brain, will be tough for AI to solve JUAN GAERTNER/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY The progress AI has made in mathematics this year is nothing short of extraordinary. In January, I was impressed to see relatively minor open problems tackled with the help of AI . Now, AI is being used to solve the hardest problems in maths . The obvious next question is, if AI can do this, is there anything it can’t do? That is the inference that the AI companies want us to make, but, in reality, the answer is much more nuanced. Read more Mathematicians are amazed by ‘holy grail’ proof of Riemann hypothesis We see this messaging in claims that AI can “solve X”, where X is any field of human endeavour you care to name. Biology is a big one. “Cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness – these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” said Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei while promoting the company’s recent initial public offering . “I think one day maybe we can cure all disease with the help of AI,” said Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, last year , adding that this could be “within the next decade or so”. This phenomenon isn’t new: I call it “physicist brain”, after the propensity for physicists to wade into areas outside their expertise and declare simple solutions. More broadly, it is called Nobel disease , after the many Nobel prizewinners who have gone on to make, shall we say, less evidenced-backed claims. In general, there is a tendency to think that if an intelligent person is good at one thing, they are good at many other things that require intelligence. What is different now is that trillion-dollar companies and large swathes of the global economy now depend on this being true of artificial intelligence. Advertisement To be clear, I think we must now admit that AI is better at solving open mathematical problems than any human, and that this has happened faster than anyone ever expected. When I first saw the news in September that the Navier-Stokes problem had been solved by OpenAI , I felt stunned. We had entered a new world. With the announcement of the Riemann hypothesis proof this week, I felt sick and had to go and have a lie-down. These were intellectual Everests I have marvelled at since my teenage years, conquered by a machine far sooner than anyone expected. You may have read my recent piece forecasting the future in 2096 – an early draft had a line, later removed, about three Millennium Prize Problems being solved by AI in the 2030s. We’ve had two this year alone. But maths isn’t biology. Yes, we have seen advances like AlphaFold, Deepmind’s AI that can predict the structure of proteins , but this is biology at its most mathematical, a computational puzzle. True advances in biology and medicine require studying cells, animals and people, all of which can be frustratingly illogical and uncooperative.
